residue.text: Source-bound deferred diagnostics: stage1 and INV propose identical select/refresh/commit actions crossing changing/frozen snapshots with row/key binding. Hypothesis: only changing-plus-row writes K5 instead of intended K2; other arms write K2. Record intended, selected and actual keys. Diagnostic arms may violate acceptance and cannot count as successful correction.

Source-bound unresolved concern: recurrence is unobserved. INV proposes enabling/suppressing mismatch-triggered refresh with matched inspection durations, then independently injecting/withholding mismatch notifications. Hypotheses distinguish refresh -> mismatch from mismatch -> refresh. Log requests separately from writes; recurrence requires a return refresh actually changing retained selection. Preserve ordinary actions, final freshness and time ceiling. Neither arrows nor an extra request establish a repeating loop.

Source-bound limits retained from stage1, ATT and INV: real editor binding, detection rates and interruption costs remain unknown; concurrency, deleted keys and load failures are outside the model. Production connectors, macros, collaboration telemetry and usability participants are unavailable. Model feasibility would not establish operational reliability, savings or human benefit.

summary.text: Consolidated acceptance: use eight invented records only; exactly K2, K5 and K7 checked and five others unchecked; no score edits; no incorrect-key write even if repaired; latest snapshot loaded; sequential completion within ten simulated minutes. Final correctness alone cannot erase an earlier miswrite.

One stipulated trace selects K2 at row 2, refreshes to S1, then writes K5 through retained row binding. Eligibility advancing without refresh leaves the loaded order intact. Stage1, ATT and INV therefore share a prospective stable-order construction; refresh-before-every-commit necessity and repeated mismatch feedback remain unproved.

Hypothesized replay, not executed: loaded S0; inspect/select K2 in 0-1, commit 1-2; inspect/select K5 in 2-3, commit 3-4; inspect/select K7 in 4-5, commit 5-6; refresh 6-7. No intermediate refresh. Prediction: only K2/K5/K7 receive checked, then S2 loads with statuses preserved by key. Log times, snapshots, selections, intended keys, every actual write and final statuses. Verified success would refute per-commit refresh necessity within this model.

Preserve the boundary check emphasized by stage1 and both concerns: S2 gives K5 and K7 score 75, with K5 first by tie ordering. Verify immutable keys and statuses after final refresh without another commit; score-only identification is ambiguous.
